To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the latest Permian global climate is more sensitive to global cooling than to global warming, which is due to the different strengths of the snow cover-albedo feedback during warm and cold climate conditions.

(1) the latest Permian palaeoclimate is characterized by a high-latitude climate zone, a boreal climate zone and a humid subtropical climate zone, which are separated from each other by a distinct climate transition belt; (2) global cooling has a higher potential of changing the palaeoclimate than global warming; and (3) global cooling has an even larger potential of changing the climate than the injection of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

the end Permian palaeoclimatic system is more sensitive to global cooling events, and thus the injection of sulphur and ash particles into the atmosphere, than to global warming events, and thus carbon greenhouse gases.
